questions.q: What abilities would Bezalel have because Yahweh filled him with his spirit?
questions.a: Yahweh filled Bezalel with his spirit to give him wisdom, understanding, and knowledge for all kinds of craftsmanship, to make artistic designs and to work in gold, silver, and bronze; also to cut and set stones and to carve wood—to do all kinds of craftsmanship.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh put skill into the hearts of all who were wise?
questions.a: Yahweh put skill into the hearts of all who were wise so that they may make all that he commanded them.

questions.q: What would happen to anyone who defiled or worked on the Sabbath?
questions.a: Everyone who defiled the Sabbath must surely be put to death. Anyone who worked on the Sabbath must surely be cut off from his people.

questions.q: Why would the Sabbath always be a sign between Yahweh and the Israelites?
questions.a: The Sabbath would always be a sign between Yahweh and the Israelites, for in six days Yahweh made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed.

questions.q: Who wrote the two tablets of covenant decrees?
questions.a: Yahweh gave Moses two tablets of covenant decrees written on by Yahweh’s own hand.

commentary.text: Bezaleel and Aholiab are appointed and qualified for the work of the tabernacle.
Moses receives the tables of the law.

Verses 1–11 The Israelites, who had been masons and bricklayers in Egypt, were not qualified for curious workmanship; but the Spirit who gave the apostles utterance in divers tongues, miraculously gave Bezaleel and Aholiab the skill that was wanting. The honour which comes from God, is always attended with a work to be done; to be employed for God is high honour. Those whom God calls to any service, he will find or make fit for it. The Lord gives different gifts to different persons; let each mind his proper work, diligently remembering that whatever wisdom any one possesses, the Lord put it in the heart, to do his commandments.

Orders were now given that a tabernacle should be set up for the service of God. But they must not think that the nature of the work, and the haste that was required, would justify them in working at it on sabbath days. The Hebrew word /shabath/ signifies rest, or ceasing from labour. The thing signified by the sabbath is that rest in glory which remains for the people of God; therefore the moral obligation of the sabbath must continue, till time is swallowed up in eternity.

The law was written in tables of stone, to show how lasting it is: to denote likewise the hardness of our hearts; one might more easily write on stone, than write any thing good on our corrupt natural hearts. It was written with the finger of God; by his will and power. God only can write his law in the heart: he gives a heart of flesh; then, by his Spirit, which is the finger of God, writes his will in the heart, 2Co 3:3.
